Consult Summary:
- Acute diarrhoea for 3 days with associated abdominal pain and one episode of vomiting; patient remains able to drink with no clear dehydration.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Diarrhoea for about 3 days, ongoing, sometimes watery/loose with abdominal pain; one episode of vomiting; no apparent blood or mucus in stool.
- Timeline: Started 3 days ago; initially expected to resolve quickly but has persisted.
- Symptom details: Diarrhoea 4–5 times per day; stool consistency varies (water and loose); appetite reduced; still drinking fluids; no high fever reported beyond “a little bit” of fever; no prolonged vomiting or inability to keep fluids down.
- Exposures: No recent travel or suspicious food intake reported.
- Associated symptoms: Abdominal pain; one episode of vomiting; appetite diminished but able to drink; no reported blood or mucus in stool.
- Review of systems: No definite fever; no dehydration observed clinically; patient able to maintain oral intake.
- Relevant negatives: No blood in stool; no mucus in stool; no overt dehydration at present; no other systemic symptoms noted.
- Additional notes: Patient reports a history of asthma; patient uses an inhaler (name variably reported as Lexapro/Laxepro in conversation); no other medications reported; no known drug allergies.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma (history; uses inhaler)
- No other medical conditions documented in dialogue

Medications:
- Inhaler for asthma (name reported inconsistently as Lexapro/Laxepro; dose/route/frequency not documented)
- No other medications documented
- Allergies: None reported

Social History:
- Not documented in transcript

Family History:
- Father had hypertension
- Father died of bowel cancer at age 62 (ten years ago)

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented
- General/ hydration: Patient appears not dehydrated; able to drink fluids
- Abdominal exam: Not described in transcript
- Other: No additional exam findings documented

Investigations:
- No investigations or test results obtained or reported

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1:
- Assessment: Acute diarrhoea for 3 days with abdominal pain; patient functioning with adequate fluid intake; no dehydration evident at this time; no blood in stool reported.
- Plan:
  - Hydration and fluids: Continue oral fluids; consider over-the-counter Dioralyte to replace lost salts.
  - Diet: Start a soft diet during diarrhoea (easily digested foods such as crackers, toast, jam). Avoid dairy, fish, meat, and eggs while diarrhoea persists.
  - Diet progression: If diarrhoea improves and there is tolerance of soft diet for about 48 hours with no diarrhoea, begin with boiled vegetables and mashed foods; after another 48 hours of tolerating soft foods and no diarrhoea, gradually reintroduce meat, eggs, fish.
  - Probiotics: Yogurt (probiotic-containing) may help restore gut flora.
  - Avoidance: Milk avoidance suggested during diarrhoea; yogurt acceptable as probiotic source.
  - Over-the-counter remedy: Dioralyte advised to replenish electrolytes.
  - Red flags and when to seek care urgently: If diarrhoea persists beyond 1 week or if blood appears in stool (stool sample may be required); if diarrhoea occurs 6–8 times per day or worse (signs of dehydration) may require hospital visit; contact patient if any of these occur.
  - Education and documentation: All information provided is available in the patient app notes for reference.

General Plan items:
- Follow-up: Reassess if symptoms persist beyond 1 week or worsen; contact care team if dehydration develops or red flags arise.
- Documentation: Notes to be stored in patient app for reference.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (no vitals documented)
  - Full review of systems (limited negative/positive findings)
  - Complete medication reconciliation beyond inhaler name (no dosing/route/frequency)
  - Social history details (smoking, alcohol, substance use, housing, access to care) not documented
  - Stool testing plan details beyond general thresholds (no stool results yet)
- Internal conflicts:
  - Inhaler name confusion: patient stated “Lexapro” and “Laxepro”; physician noted uncertainty. Conflict noted.
- Transcript quality:
  - Dialogue contains misstatements and ambiguity around inhaler name; some wording is informal and could benefit clarification. Overall content sufficient to establish primary diarrhoea management plan.
